Chapter 12
How Many Kinds Of Soldiery There Are, And Concerning Mercenaries

I have already talked in detail about the characteristics of the different types of principalities I proposed to discuss at the beginning. I have also examined the reasons why they succeed or fail. Along the way, I showed the methods many people have used to acquire and hold them. Now, it is time for me to discuss in general terms the methods of attack and defense that apply to each of these states.

We have seen how necessary it is for a prince to build solid foundations. Otherwise, he will inevitably face ruin. The most important foundations for all states, whether they are new, old, or mixed, are good laws and good armies. You cannot have good laws if a state is not well armed. It naturally follows that where states are well armed, they will also have good laws. Therefore, I will leave the topic of laws out of this discussion and focus purely on armies.

The armed forces a prince uses to defend his state are either his own, mercenaries, auxiliaries, or a mix of these. Mercenaries and auxiliaries are both useless and highly dangerous. If a prince builds his state on mercenary forces, he will never be secure or safe. These troops are divided, ambitious, undisciplined, and completely disloyal. They act brave among friends, but turn cowardly in the face of the enemy. They neither fear God nor keep faith with men. With mercenaries, your destruction is only delayed as long as the attack is delayed. During times of peace, these soldiers rob you. During war, they let the enemy rob you. The truth is, mercenaries have no motivation to stay on the battlefield other than a small paycheck. That tiny wage is simply not enough to make them willing to die for you. They are happy to be your soldiers as long as you are not fighting an actual war. But the moment war breaks out, they will either desert you or run away from the enemy. I do not have to try very hard to prove this point. The current ruin of Italy has been caused by nothing else but relying entirely on mercenary armies for many years. At first, these mercenaries put on a good show and seemed brave when fighting against other Italians. But when foreign invaders arrived, they showed their true colors. This is exactly how King Charles of France was able to conquer Italy so easily, simply marking up the houses where his troops would stay with a piece of chalk. A certain priest once said that our sins were the cause of our downfall, and he told the truth. However, they were not the spiritual sins he imagined, but the military blunders I have just described. And since these were the sins of princes, it is the princes who have ultimately paid the price.

Let me explain further why these forces are completely flawed. Mercenary commanders are either highly skilled or they are not. If they are highly skilled, you can never trust them. They will always try to seize power for themselves, either by turning against you, their employer, or by attacking others contrary to your orders. On the other hand, if the commander is incompetent, he will just ruin you the old-fashioned way by losing the war.

You might argue that any armed commander will act this way, whether he is a mercenary or not. My answer is that military forces must be commanded directly by either a prince or a republic. A prince should go to the battlefield in person and take on the role of the commander himself. A republic must send its own citizens. If the republic sends a man who turns out to be incompetent, they should replace him immediately. If he proves capable, they must control him strictly with laws so he does not overstep his authority. Experience proves that only princes and republics with their own armies achieve true greatness, while mercenaries do nothing but cause immense damage. Furthermore, it is much harder for a single citizen to take over a republic if it is armed with its own troops, compared to a republic that relies on foreign forces. Rome and Sparta remained armed and free for centuries. The Swiss are heavily armed today, and they are completely free.

If you want an example from ancient history, look at the Carthaginians. They were violently oppressed by their own mercenary soldiers right after their first war with the Romans, even though the Carthaginians had their own citizens acting as commanders. Consider the Thebans as well. After the death of Epaminondas, they made Philip of Macedon the commander of their army. After he won the war for them, he immediately stripped them of their liberty.

When Duke Filippo died, the Milanese hired Francesco Sforza to fight the Venetians. After he crushed the enemy at the Battle of Caravaggio, Sforza betrayed his employers and allied with the Venetians to conquer Milan. Similarly, his father, Muzio Sforza, was hired by Queen Johanna of Naples. He abruptly abandoned her, leaving her completely unprotected. To save her kingdom, she was forced to throw herself into the arms of the King of Aragon. You might point out that the Venetians and Florentines successfully expanded their empires using mercenary armies in the past, and their commanders defended them instead of making themselves princes. I reply that the Florentines were simply favored by luck. Among the capable commanders they could have feared, some failed to conquer, some faced strong opposition, and others directed their ambitions elsewhere. Giovanni Acuto was one who did not conquer. Because he never won a decisive victory, his loyalty was never truly tested. But everyone must admit that if he had conquered, the Florentines would have been completely at his mercy. Sforza was always opposed by the Bracceschi forces, keeping both factions locked in a stalemate. Eventually, Francesco Sforza focused his ambitions on Lombardy, while Braccio turned his sights against the Church and the Kingdom of Naples. But let us look at what happened just a short time ago. The Florentines appointed Pagolo Vitelli as their commander. He was a highly cautious man who had risen from a commoner to achieve massive renown. If he had managed to capture the city of Pisa, nobody can deny that the Florentines would have been forced to do whatever he wanted. If he had switched sides to join their enemies, Florence would have been defenseless. By keeping him, they would have had to obey him. Now consider the Venetians. If you examine their achievements, you will see they operated safely and gloriously as long as they fought with their own men. This was back when they fought at sea, where their nobles and commoners fought bravely together. But when they started launching military campaigns on land, they abandoned this strategy and adopted the dangerous Italian custom of hiring mercenaries. In the early days of their land expansion, Venice did not have much to fear from their commanders because they owned little territory and had an overwhelming reputation. But when they expanded further under the command of Carmignuola, they realized their massive mistake. They saw he was a brilliant commander after he defeated the Duke of Milan. However, they soon noticed he was growing reluctant to fight. The Venetians realized they could not win any more battles under his command. But they could not simply fire him, because they were terrified of losing the territory they had just gained. To secure themselves, they had no choice but to murder him. Later, Venice hired other mercenary captains like Bartolomeo da Bergamo, Roberto da San Severino, and the Count of Pitigliano. With commanders like these, the Venetians had to worry about catastrophic losses rather than any new gains. This nightmare became reality at the Battle of Vaila, where in a single day they lost everything they had spent eight hundred years painstakingly acquiring. This is the reality of mercenary armies: they bring slow, delayed, and insignificant conquests, but massive, sudden, and devastating losses.

Since these examples have brought us back to Italy, a country that has been controlled by mercenaries for many years, I want to explore this issue more deeply. By understanding how the mercenary system began and spread, we will be better prepared to destroy it. You must understand that the Holy Roman Empire has recently lost its authority in Italy. At the same time, the Pope has gained significant political power, and the country has splintered into many smaller states. This happened because many major cities rebelled against their nobles. These nobles, once backed by the Emperor, used to oppress the people. The Church encouraged these rebellions to increase its own political power, while in other cities, powerful private citizens simply seized control and made themselves princes. As a result, Italy fell entirely into the hands of the Church and various republics. Since the Church was run by priests and the republics were run by civilians with zero military experience, both groups started hiring foreign mercenaries to fight their wars.

The first commander who brought real prestige to these mercenary forces was Alberigo da Conio from Romagna. Men like Braccio and Sforza, who eventually became the undisputed masters of Italy, were trained in his school of warfare. After them came all the other mercenary captains who have commanded Italy's armies up to the present day. The ultimate result of their so-called brilliance is that Italy has been overrun by Charles of France, looted by Louis of France, devastated by Ferdinand of Spain, and utterly humiliated by the Swiss. The guiding strategy of these mercenary captains was to ruin the reputation of foot soldiers in order to boost their own prestige. They did this because they had no land of their own and lived entirely on their paychecks. They could not afford to feed a massive infantry, and a small infantry commanded no respect. So, they relied on cavalry instead. With a relatively small force of horsemen, they could still demand high pay and respect. Things got so absurd that in an army of twenty thousand men, you would not even find two thousand foot soldiers. On top of this, these commanders used every trick in the book to avoid fatigue and danger for themselves and their men. They stopped killing each other in battle. Instead, they just took prisoners and released them without even demanding a ransom. They refused to attack cities at night, and the city garrisons refused to launch night raids against their camps. They stopped building trenches or defensive walls around their camps, and they absolutely refused to fight during the winter. All of this cowardly behavior was perfectly legal under their military rules. They designed this system for one specific purpose: to avoid hard work and danger. Because of them, Italy has been dragged into slavery and total disgrace.
